newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia wants to complete privatisation by mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: Latvia wants to complete privatisation by mid-1998.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele unveiled a draft government programme on Tuesday that seeks to complete privatisations by mid-1998 and increase the state's infrastructure investment by 50 percent in the 1998 state budget.
President Guntis Ulmanis reappointed Shkele to form a new government last week, following Shkele's surprise resignation two weeks ago.
"By mid-1998, privatisation should in principle be completed, including large companies, making wide use of vouchers in public offers," the draft programme said.

Shkele's first government pushed ahead with privatisation, putting major transport and energy companies such as the Latvian Shipping company, energy firm Latvenergo and gas supplier Latvian Gas on the block.
"The 1998 state budget should include a 50-percent rise in state investment in infrastructure," the programme added.
It also said a body should be set up to control tariffs set by monopoly state-owned utilities.
The new government also intends to restructure the energy sector's debts to improve payment discipline and enhance energy saving investment.
It also wants to start restructuring state-owned Latvian Railways this year and by the end of 1997, to have privatised around 20 percent of apartments.
Shkele first came to power at the end of 1995, vowing to pull Latvia out of the financial mess that hit after a mid-1995 banking crisis.
Shkele does not belong to any political party. Instead he is a a businessman, appointed for his financial expertise and free-market credentials.
